glass_priya: Pattern: I incorrectly guessed nightstand_b1 for a late-night query (20:43 on day 11), likely over-weighting the previous day's late-night evidence (22:14 on day 10). Reality: At 20:43 on day 11, it was at kitchen_table_k1. This contradicts my previous note that "kitchen is incorrect." The item clearly moves between living room (coffee_table_l1), bedroom (nightstand_b1), and kitchen (kitchen_table_k1). Next time: Do not exclude kitchen spots. Check kitchen_table_k1, coffee_table_l1, and nightstand_b1 with equal weight for evening/late-night queries. Look for specific evidence of movement among these three spots.

razor_priya: Pattern: I defaulted to medicine_cabinet_ba1 based on day 9 evidence, ignoring the rotation. Reality: At 07:00 on day 10, it was at bathroom_shelf_ba1. It rotates among shelf, sink, and medicine cabinet without a fixed daily schedule. Next time: Do not default to any single spot. Check all three bathroom spots (shelf, sink, medicine cabinet) with equal weight, prioritizing the most recent confirmed location if available, but be prepared for it to have moved to any of the other two.

mug_priya: Pattern: I assumed it was in cupboard_k1 in the morning. Reality: At 07:27 on day 9, it was at kitchen_table_k1. Previous notes suggested desk_b1 for evenings, but morning location is distinct. Next time: Check kitchen_table_k1 for morning queries; do not assume cupboard_k1.

General Note: Avoid rigid location rules for glass_priya, mug_priya, and razor_priya. These items move frequently. For glass_priya, valid spots include kitchen_table_k1, coffee_table_l1, and nightstand_b1; do not exclude kitchen. For mug_priya, kitchen_table_k1 is a common morning spot. For razor_priya, all three bathroom spots are valid. Always prioritize recent specific evidence over general patterns, but recognize that "recent" may be from a different day if the item rotates.
